title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is very faint. It is evidently a first draft of the text that is rewritten cleanly on page 26, and the reading below leans on that page. It opens with a displayed map pi_1(Spec k, xi) -> G, with something written underneath it. In modern terms this is the Galois representation landing in the motivic Galois group, i.e. the l-adic realization seen as a homomorphism from the arithmetic fundamental group into G(Q_l) (or into the motivic group's l-adic points). The underlined heading on the right appears to read something like 'structures filtrées et comparaison avec Betti' (unsure).

Then: let k ⊂ C and consider a tannakian category M of motives of finite type over k (possibly mixed). It has two natural fibre functors:
(1) T_DR : M -> Modf(k), de Rham realization, which carries the Hodge filtration;
(2) T_B (the machine transcription reads T_l) : M -> Modf(Q), Betti realization, which depends on the embedding k ⊂ C.
(3) The comparison isomorphism T_B ⊗_Q C ≃ T_DR ⊗_k C.

With G = Aut_⊗(T_B), compare T_DR with T_B ⊗_Q k. This gives a right G_k-torsor P = Isom_⊗(T_B ⊗ k, T_DR) (4), from which T_DR is recovered by contracted product (5). The comparison isomorphism (3) is a canonical complex point of P, written alpha (or phi) ∈ P(C). A bracketed marginal remark seems to say that the data (G, P, phi) reconstruct M together with (1)-(3).

The lower part introduces how to recover the filtration on T_DR, and hence the Hodge structure on T_B (the bigrading of T_B ⊗ C):
- T_Hdg = gr T_DR, a bigraded fibre functor (6);
- the inner form G'_k = ad(P) = Aut_⊗(T_DR) (7);
- presumably the subgroup of G'_k preserving the filtration and inducing the identity on the graded pieces, a unipotent radical of a parabolic (8).

In modern language this is the period torsor of a motive or a category of motives. P is the torsor of 'formal periods' (Kontsevich-Zagier / André), and the comparison point is the complex point whose coordinates are the periods. Grothendieck's period conjecture states that this point is generic, i.e. that the Zariski closure of the point over Q is all of P.
errors: The page is mostly illegible. The machine transcription's T_l is most likely T_B (Betti), as on page 26, although an l-adic variant cannot be fully excluded. As far as can be judged, nothing on the page is mathematically wrong; it is a draft.

ideas.what: Torsor P = Isom_⊗(T_B⊗k, T_DR) under the motivic Galois group G_k, with the comparison isomorphism giving a canonical point in P(C)
ideas.modern_name: Period torsor / torsor of formal periods; Grothendieck period conjecture setting
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (period conjecture, via the 1966 de Rham paper footnote and Lang's book); developed by Deligne (Hodge cycles, 1982), André (2004), Kontsevich-Zagier (2001)
ideas.where_published: Period conjecture alluded to in Grothendieck, 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (1966) footnote; the torsor formulation appears in later literature (Deligne-Milne, André)

ideas.what: Galois representation as a homomorphism pi_1(Spec k) -> motivic Galois group
ideas.modern_name: l-adic realization of the motivic Galois group; Galois image contained in the motivic group (Mumford-Tate / Tate conjecture context)
ideas.where_published: Saavedra Rivano, Catégories tannakiennes (1972); Serre's motivic Galois group writings

ideas.what: Hodge filtration recovered via gr T_DR as a bigraded fibre functor; inner form ad(P) = Aut_⊗(T_DR); subgroup preserving the filtration and acting trivially on gr
ideas.modern_name: Filtered fibre functors and the unipotent radical of a parabolic; tannakian description of Hodge structures

missed.claim: This is an early (1965 dossier), explicit tannakian formulation of the period torsor: P = Isom_⊗(T_B⊗k, T_DR) with the comparison isomorphism as a complex point. It is stated for a possibly mixed category of motives, with the claim that (G, P, phi) reconstruct the realizations. It documents that Grothendieck had the torsor picture behind the period conjecture, not just the transcendence-degree statement.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority detail for the period-torsor formulation usually written down later (Deligne, André, Kontsevich-Zagier). It is not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The period torsor and the period conjecture are attributed to Grothendieck in this era, so the content is expected. The explicit tannakian torsor with a complex point, the possible mention of mixed motives, and the use of a filtered fibre functor in a 1965 draft are a mildly notable documentary detail. The page is largely illegible.
